Infrastructure, Institutions, and the Conservation of Biodiversity in India
venue: Journal of the Association of Environmental and Resource Economists
abstract: Anthropogenic land use change is the leading threat to biodiversity. This study examines how infrastructure expansion degrades biodiversity and what role local institutions play in mitigating species loss. Combining new data from India on infrastructure-driven deforestation with 1 million bird-watching diaries, I document a sizable infrastructure-biodiversity trade-off. Forest encroachment by transport, irrigation, resettlement camps, and mining projects accounts for 20% of total species loss. The trade-off is especially acute in already-fragmented landscapes, and species diversity does not recover in the medium run. Yet the extent of species loss is more than halved when local institutions enable marginalized communities, who are often excluded from project planning, to mobilize around their interests. Informed consent between developers and tribal communities is a key mechanism, underscoring the importance of inclusive institutions for balancing development and conservation.
abstract_zh: 人为的土地利用变化是生物多样性面临的首要威胁。本研究考察了基础设施扩张如何损害生物多样性，以及地方制度在缓解物种损失中所发挥的作用。我结合印度基础设施驱动的森林砍伐新数据与100万份观鸟日记，记录了基础设施与生物多样性之间相当显著的权衡关系。交通、灌溉、安置营地和采矿项目造成的森林侵占，占物种损失总量的20%。这种权衡在本已破碎化的景观中尤为突出，而且物种多样性在中期内并不会恢复。然而，当地方制度使通常被排除在项目规划之外的边缘化社区能够动员起来维护自身利益时，物种损失的程度可减少一半以上。开发者与部落社区之间的知情同意是关键机制，这凸显了包容性制度对于平衡发展与保护的重要性。

title: Ruling The Roost: Avian Species Reclaim Urban Habitat During India's COVID-19 Lockdown
Saving the world from your couch: The heterogeneous medium-run benefits of COVID-19 lockdowns on air pollution
abstract: In Spring 2020, COVID-19 led to an unprecedented halt in public and economic life across the globe. In an otherwise tragic time, this provides a unique natural experiment to investigate the environmental impact of such a (temporary) ‘de-globalization’. Here, we estimate the medium-run impact of a battery of COVID-19 related lockdown measures on air quality across 162 countries, going beyond the existing short-run estimates from a limited number of countries. In doing so, we leverage a new dataset categorizing lockdown measures and tracking their implementation and release, extending to 31 August 2020. We find that domestic and international lockdown measures overall led to a decline in PM2.5 pollution by 45% and 35%, respectively. This substantial impact persists in the medium-run, even as lockdowns are lifted, there is, however, substantial heterogeneity across different types of lockdown measures, different countries, and different sources of pollution. We show that some country trajectories are much more appealing (with fewer COVID-19 casualties, less economic downturn and bigger pollution reductions) than others. Our results have important policy implications and highlight the potential to ‘build back better’ a sustainable economy where pollution can be curbed in a less economically costly way than during the COVID-19 pandemic.
abstract_zh: 2020年春季，COVID-19导致全球公共生活和经济活动出现前所未有的停滞。在这一本身充满悲剧的时期，它为考察这种（暂时性的）“去全球化”对环境的影响提供了一个独特的自然实验。在此，我们估计了一系列与COVID-19相关的封锁措施对162个国家空气质量的中期影响，超越了基于少数国家的既有短期估计。为此，我们利用了一个新数据集，该数据集对封锁措施进行了分类，并追踪其实施与解除的情况，时间延伸至2020年8月31日。我们发现，国内和国际封锁措施总体上分别使PM2.5污染下降了45%和35%。这一显著影响在中期内持续存在，即便封锁措施已经解除。不过，不同类型的封锁措施、不同国家以及不同污染来源之间存在显著的异质性。我们表明，一些国家的发展路径更具吸引力（COVID-19死亡人数更少、经济衰退更轻、污染减少幅度更大），而另一些则不然。我们的结果具有重要的政策含义，并凸显了“重建得更好”（build back better）的潜力，即以比COVID-19大流行期间成本更低的经济方式，构建一个能够抑制污染的可持续经济体。
